profile.headline: Security Software Engineer @ Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory | Developing Secure Software Solutions
profile.summary:
A graduate of the University of the Pacific with a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Applied Mathematics, currently contributing as a Security Software Engineer at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory. The role encompasses active participation in developing and maintaining the Identity Management software for the HPC center, ensuring robust security through role-based access control and mentoring new team members.  

The position also involves managing Java software for RSA SecurID token administration and leading the migration efforts toward high-availability services. With a focus on application security and SaaS, the work emphasizes building secure and reliable systems to support the Lab's mission.

positions.title: Security Software Engineer
positions.description:
I wear many hats at the Lab's HPC center! Here are a few:

- My team (the Security Technologies Team) created and managed the Identity Management software for LLNL's HPC center, which included a transition to role based access control. I was a main contributor to the original project and now work to maintain it by implementing new features, addressing bug reports and user questions, and mentoring newer employees while they get started on the project.
- I maintain Java software to manage thousands of RSA SecurID tokens for Lab-wide use. 
- I'm responsible for our migration to make all our services high availability
positions.insights: Python (Programming Language), Network Security and +5 skills

positions.title: Computing Intern
positions.description:
LLNL's internship programs are primarily focused on learning and career development opportunities for students. As such, I spent my first summer at LLNL learning how to create malicious Docker containers and run penetration tests on high-performance computing systems in order to test whether or not my detection algorithms would catch the malicious activity. My detection algorithm ran via the ELK stack (Elastic, Logstash, and Kibana). During my next summer, I worked with developers at various national labs and IBM on High Performance Storage System, which is used to indefinitely and securely store exabytes of data produced by supercomputing facilities. A list of my accomplishments at LLNL can be found below:
● Developed scalable software in C for High Performance Storage System (HPSS)
● Created containerized applications and used Elastic tools to monitor their performance
● Performed and automated machine learning tasks for anomaly detection
● Ran applications on High Performance Computing clusters
● Developed software to interact with the Github API
● Created a proxy SMTP server in Python
● Formally presented a poster and performed a demonstration of relevant work

positions.title: Data Science Research Intern
positions.description: I was selected to participate in the Summer Research Opportunities Program at MSU as my first "out of class" computer science experience. It was in this position that I learned how to create data science algorithms and investigate/predict the behavior of an online trading network called Bonanza. To do so, I parsed data from large files with 100,000+ entries and analyzed it using sparse matrices in Python. I then wrote a research paper about my results and presented a poster at a regional symposium. I chose data science as my first internship experience as it was an excellent blend between my math and programming passions and enabled me to get hands on experience using Python.

volunteerExperiences.description: QFTT is a volunteer organization that matches tutors from the University of the Pacific's Powell Scholars program to students at Stagg High School who are looking for assistance with test preparation. While it was originally designed for the SAT and ACT, students will soon be able to ask for help with college applications and financial aid forms as well.
